scoring_justification: Recomputing from raw DFT energies is infeasible because the output contract does not include the slab and interface total energies; the checker cannot rerun DFT. The paper's trends (relative surface energies, adhesion ordering, negative and constant interfacial energies) are robust and verifiable from the reported CSV tables.

hidden_assets.purpose: Qualitative trends for surface energy, work of adhesion, and interfacial energy determined from the paper's figures and tables (Fig. 1, Table 3, Fig. 5).
hidden_assets.generation_method: extracted expected physical trends (C-surface > Al-surface; W_ad ordering; interfacial energies negative, C- < Al, constant with mu) without numeric gold values.
hidden_assets.why_not_fabricated: The trends are the paper's explicit conclusions, not invented numbers; they provide a verifiable structural test.

outputs.description: Surface energies of Al4C3(0001) C- and Al-terminated slabs as a function of Al chemical potential relative to bulk.
Ideal work of adhesion for the four Mg(0002)/Al4C3(0001) interface models.
Interfacial energies of the four interface models as a function of Al chemical potential.

output_contract.notes: All energies are in J/m². The chemical potential range and conversion factors are provided in the instructions. The agent must re-run all DFT calculations and use the derived total energies to compute these outputs.

steps.description: Verify surface energy trends: C-terminated > Al-terminated and both positive over the entire chemical potential range.
Verify work of adhesion ordering: C-OT > C-HCP, C-OT > Al-OT, C-OT > Al-HCP; all values positive.

Verify interfacial energies: all negative, C-terminated models give lower (more negative) values than Al-terminated at each chemical potential, and gamma is constant (variance < 1e-2) across mu for each model.
